claims: binding:name-collision compares Ossie's normalized form: two tables that are not regular identifiers and differ only in case, such as fin.cust and FIN.CUST, are accepted as two tables, and two regular names that differ only in case, such as cust and Cust, are still refused.
_quoted and the collision check share one helper, normalized_identifier, so a pair of names the exporter writes as one identifier is always refused and a pair it writes as two is never refused.
The size bound covers the two new relational files, so a large model whose three files fitted can now stop with ossie:output-size; the release note says so and names the remedies.
Plan r3 appends eighteen close amendments in section 11, each naming the record that raised it, and the approved r2 text is kept.
The close results give, for each completion predicate, evidence that would fail if it were false, and every open question is closed, carried with an owner, or an accepted residual.

The close record states that the owner has not ruled the close, that external acceptance is missing, that the repairs made after the panel are unreviewed, and that the oracle lane's consumer test was not run.
No public text in the change names a downstream project, customer or reporter.
